A Run opens with 4 of: **Pew**, **Blam**, **Snipe**, **Ring**, **Fireball**, **Zaap**.

## Glade (T1/T2)

The opening biome, where the player learns the systems and fills out a first kit. Enemy density is low, variety is high, stakes are gentle. The starting glade is pure onboarding, and the veggie glade brings in the plant roster and its Miniboss.

### Starting glade

Onboarding, and the Spawn zone: the first roster enemies are taught one at a time before anything mixes.

### Veggie glade

Brings in the plant roster: thornthrower and rosebud join the Glade's own, and the thornmess waits as the Zone's Miniboss.

## Deepwood (T3)

The second biome, tuned to pressure long-range, squishy builds and push the player into close quarters. Enemies have far more health and hit harder. It has two Zones: the animal deepwood, and the small mimic pocket. The insect one is still a proposal and stays in the ideas section below; the fungal one left the deepwood entirely and became the Mycelium, a Side biome of its own.

### Animal deepwood

The bulk of the forest. Each of the eight mechanics is taught alone before its enemies mix, the six family variations come later, and the three rares and the gnarlking sit on top. The variations are deliberately kept apart, so seeing all three moths or all three snakes means going looking for them.

### Mimic deepwood

A small pocket of props with eyes: the bush that reveals, the harasser that blinks, then the two logs that are bombs, each taught on its own before it mixes with the shared pool, so the mine is never the only thing asking for your attention. Its three rares each escort the common they are a variant of.

## Mycelium (T3)

The fungal Side biome hanging off the deepwood, in three Zones: clusters, hollows and sporefields. Spore clouds are the floor both sides fight over.

# ideas

## Deepwood Zones (T3)

The deepwood splits into three Zones in encounter order — animal, mimic, insect — over a
shared pool of natives that appears in all three. The **shared pool and the animal and mimic
Zones are built and spawning**; both are in the catalogue above. What follows is the one
that isn't. It adds three commons, three rares (almost all variants of another enemy) and its
boss: 16 per Zone. Commons drop T2, rares guarantee T3, bosses drop their T3 signatures.

A fourth Zone, fungal, was planned here and **left** — it is the Mycelium now, a Side biome of
its own hanging off the deepwood.

Each Zone introduces at most three new mechanics; later ones reuse and combine earlier
ones (ledger in enemies.md). Spells still waiting on this one: Halo. Slurp and Vroop are
earmarked for the hive. Reserved for future T3 biomes: Kaboom, Krak, Brrr, Clang, Chomp,
Piercing Lights, Beep Boop, Nyoom, Shing, Splay, Fwoosh.
